analyzed_vuln.description: xmlParseNCNameComplex computes startPosition as an unsigned size_t offset (CUR_PTR - BASE_PTR), then keeps parsing while calling GROW, which can reallocate/move the input buffer. It later calls xmlDictLookup(ctxt->dict, BASE_PTR + startPosition, len) using the old offset against the new BASE_PTR. If the base pointer changed, BASE_PTR + startPosition can point before/after valid input, causing out-of-bounds read in xmlDictComputeFastKey (crash site in dict.c).
analyzed_vuln.conditions: In the schema harness, xmlSchemaParse -> xmlSchemaAddSchemaDoc -> xmlCtxtReadFile parses attacker-controlled XML. Input must drive NCName parsing through xmlParseNCNameComplex and trigger at least one buffer growth (GROW) while parsing that name so the input base can move. The function then interns the name via xmlDictLookup with a stale offset-derived pointer, leading to global-buffer-overflow during hash computation.
